findings.title: Do not cache devices before admission succeeds
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still populates the local cache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When a new device is rejected because the limit is reached, its cache entry remains. Retrying with the same device ID returns nil from the cache and successfully authenticates for the next 29 minutes, despite the device never being admitted. Cache only successful admissions and add a test that repeats a rejected request.

findings.title: Make the limit check and device admission atomic
findings.body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without serialization. If two new devices arrive when one slot remains, both can observe a count below the limit and both are inserted and authenticated. This also occurs across Grafana replicas, and the excess devices continue to be accepted by the update-only path. Serialize the count and admission at the database level so concurrent requests cannot exceed the configured limit.

findings.title: Handle requests without a device ID when enforcing the limit
findings.body: Authentication relies exclusively on TagDevice returning ErrDeviceLimitReached, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is missing. An anonymous client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and continue accessing Grafana without being counted or checked, even when the configured device limit is full. Define and enforce admission for requests without a device ID rather than treating skipped tracking as successful admission.
